learning_outcomes.text: Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being capable of integrating them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and use of the principles of strength of materials.

syllabus_topics: INTRODUCTION TO STRENGTH OF MATERIALS
Concept and objectives of Strength of Materials
Definition of rigid body, elastic body, and true body
Definition of mechanical prism
Static equilibrium and elastic equilibrium
Isostatic and hyperstatic systems
Calculation of forces derived from the action of a system of forces on a mechanical prism
Types of stresses and deformations. Relationship between stress and deformation. Hooke's Law
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO AXIAL FORCES
Elements subjected to tension-compression with isostatic support
Calculation of stresses and deformations. Axial force and stress diagrams
Elements subjected to tension-compression with hyperstatic support. Equation of deformation compatibility. Thermal and assembly defect stresses
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO BENDING
Pure bending. Simplification hypotheses. Simple bending and symmetric bending
Normal stress distribution: Navier's Law. Tangential stresses
Bending moment and shear force diagrams
Resistance equation. Profile calculation
Deformations in elements subjected to bending
Differential equation of the elastic curve
Mohr's theorems. Conjugate beam
Calculation of single-span hyperstatic beams
BUCKLING
Stability analysis
Euler's formula
Concepts of buckling length and slenderness
Application of CTE in the calculation of elements at risk of buckling
CALCULATION AND DESIGN OF ELEMENTS SUBJECTED TO TORSION
Torsion in circular and annular sections. Power transmission shafts
Shear stress distribution. Torsion resistance equation
Torsional moment diagrams
Deformations in torsion
assessment_rules: To pass the course, a weighted minimum of 5 out of 10 points is required, except if a maximum grade is obtained in the global exam, which automatically grants a 10 for the course. Laboratory practices account for 10% of the final grade and must be completed successfully. In the progressive evaluation path, if all three partial controls are passed (>=5), the final grade is 10% practices + 90% average of partials; otherwise, it is 10% practices + 30% partials average + 60% final exam (requiring >=4 in the final). For the ordinary global call, a minimum of 5 overall and >=4 in the global exam is needed. For the extraordinary call, a minimum of 5 overall (10% practices + 90% exam) and >=5 in the exam is required.
